A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GTR and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. All 19 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v3 support comparison, including relocated and revised supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSO and OmniObject3D evaluations, reconstruction examples, and geometry, texture, encoder, and training-data ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds baseline comparisons and a normal-loss experiment.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.1 replace opacity regularization with normal-map supervision, introduced after training stabilizes with the generator frozen. v1 discusses normal supervision only as future work. The architecture, two-stage reconstruction framework, and per-instance texture refinement remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The mixed Objaverse/internal training data, GSO and OmniObject3D benchmarks, and generated-image applications remain. However, Figure 6 removes v1's explicitly identified real-world-image demonstration involving two plush birds; v3 does not identify an equivalent real-photo application example. This slightly narrows documented scenario coverage.

E2.justification: v3 substantially broadens comparisons by adding SV3D and CRM to the GSO results in Table 1 and introducing a qualitative MeshLRM comparison in Figure 11. These methods were not evaluated as comparators in v1. The existing quantitative comparators remain, and OmniObject3D's comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a geometry-training control: delay normal supervision until stabilization and freeze the generator when applying it. The principal training budgets, 300 GSO and 130 OmniObject3D evaluation objects, camera trajectories, and mesh-alignment procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a normal-loss ablation and an additional geometry-refinement case in Figures 9 and 8. It removes v1's color-only versus triplane-only versus joint texture-optimization study, including Table 3 and Figure 11. Encoder and training-data ablations survive unchanged; the texture-refinement before/after display retains fewer examples.

E5.justification: The shaded PSNR training curves are identical across v1 Figures 9–10 and v3 Figures 12–13. Neither version explains those bands through a statistical procedure or supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds SV3D/CRM scores, normal-loss findings, and MeshLRM examples while removing texture-component results and revising qualitative examples. Main GTR benchmark scores match after rounding. Small non-rounding changes include GSO LRM PSNR 20.4485 to 20.446 and InstantMesh Mesh IoU 0.6457 to 0.645. v3's introductory GSO SSIM 0.94 and LPIPS 0.059 conflict with Table 1's 0.960 and 0.047.

T1.justification: The formal mesh-objective definition in Equation 3 substitutes weighted normal-map loss for weighted opacity regularization. The density-to-SDF mapping and other loss definitions remain unchanged; neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain architectural refinements, mesh-based geometry refinement, and fast per-instance texture optimization, with claims of superior reconstruction and text/image-to-3D applicability. v3's two contribution bullets regroup existing components without redefining the principal contribution or scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds normal-loss instability and improved surface quality to the discussion. Appendix B replaces v1's limitations paragraph with specific constraints concerning triplane resolution, known camera poses, and object-centric coverage. The NeuS initialization discussion disappears, while the VAE initialization analysis remains in Appendix A.

D1.justification: v3 specifies a normal-loss weight of 1 and its delayed activation and generator-freezing procedure, replacing the opacity-regularization weight of 0.5. It also changes the project-site pointer from the author's website to Snap Research's GTR page. Most architecture, optimizer, hardware, and data-processing details are retained.

R1.justification: SV3D is newly cited, and MeshLRM changes from a regularization reference to a direct visual comparator. Several references disappear, including NeuS, NeRF, AdamW, and the original Gaussian Splatting paper. The related-work organization and general positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive localized rewrites, contributions become two bullets, and the conclusion is shortened. The main-text limitations section is replaced by an appendix section. Most methodological and related-work prose retains its previous organization and wording.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: ICLR formatting replaces the preprint layout, Figure 2 gains normal outputs, and new geometry, normal-loss, and MeshLRM figures appear. Table 1 expands, Table 3 and several appendix comparisons disappear, texture examples are trimmed, normal renderings are revised, and generation galleries are consolidated and reselected.

improvement.justification: Broader GSO comparisons, a direct normal-loss ablation, and clearer applicability limits modestly strengthen the paper. These gains are tempered by removal of the useful texture-component ablation and the new introduction/Table 1 inconsistency in GSO SSIM and LPIPS. The largely retained benchmark scores do not establish a new numerical gain from the revised training.
